chunk_findings.detail: The diff rewrites the iteration/wave-loop prose and the subagent model-routing prose, but it contains no hunk updating the driver stamp. Bc9e602dd98 explicitly requires this delta to move from the stale `ddflow=0.2.0 sha=5942a35e0678` stamp to the current `ddflow=0.2.9` stamp used by the other driver deltas. After applying this diff, a drift/sync check that parses the stamp line still sees the old stamp, so the version half of the bug remains open even though the prose has changed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md:stamp

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test added to close this bug does not assert the stamp condition. If the Claude Code delta contains the new prose substrings (`ddflow next --json`, `tier:fast|balanced|deep`, the operator-stop sentence, and `event log`) but still carries the stale `ddflow=0.2.0 sha=5942a35e0678` stamp, every assertion in the test passes. The test can therefore go green while the stamp drift named in Bc9e602dd98 is still present, giving false confidence that the bug is fixed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_drift.py:test_claude_delta_carries_the_goal_wave_contract

chunk_findings.detail: This part bumps only the generated docs copy to `ddflow=0.2.9`, but the source template delta (the file drivers actually load) still lacks the stamp update and remains `ddflow=0.2.0 sha=5942a35e0678` as in the earlier untriaged finding. The manifest shows the docs copy has one extra changed line relative to the template delta, consistent with the stamp line being changed here but not in the template. A drift/sync check against the template delta therefore still sees the old stamp, so the stamp half of Bc9e602dd98 is not closed even though the docs copy now looks fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md:stamp

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression test still does not assert the driver stamp condition that Bc9e602dd98 explicitly names. If the Claude Code delta contains the new goal-wave prose (`ddflow next --json`, `tier:fast|balanced|deep`, the operator-stop sentence, and `event log`) but its stamp line remains `ddflow=0.2.0 sha=5942a35e0678`, the test passes. That gives false confidence that the bug is fixed while the version/stamp drift can persist or regress.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_driver_drift.py:test_claude_delta_carries_the_goal_wave_contract

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test still does not assert the driver-stamp condition that is part of Bc9e602dd98. It checks only four prose substrings and then asserts that the docs region body equals the template body. If the Claude Code template and its generated docs view both contain the new prose but remain stamped `ddflow=0.2.0 sha=5942a35e0678` while the other driver deltas are `ddflow=0.2.9`, every assertion in this test passes: the prose substrings are present, `view == text` holds because the docs view was regenerated from the same stale template, and no assertion compares the stamp to the current version or to the other driver deltas. The added docs/template equality therefore does not answer the earlier stamp-drift findings; the named stamp drift can remain or regress while this test remains green.
